Semantic interaction starts from rendered coordinates, not displayed text. In `src/components/SnlSyntaxTreeView.tsx`, `handleClick` locates the enclosing `data-tree-path` element, respects descendant controls that own their events, and calls `dispatchElementActivation`. That function resolves the path against the rendered tree and supplies the actual node, resolved Macro, DOM target, modifier state, and activation lease to the interaction driver.

`SnlInteractionDriver.dispatch_click` in `src/snl-react-view/interaction-driver.ts` distinguishes Ctrl from Meta and falls back to the ordinary click callback when no Ctrl callback exists. Its callbacks may be asynchronous. The view's `createActivation` gives each activation a generation-checked lease: delayed work can request deactivation without clearing a newer activation.

`EntrySurface` in `src/entry-react/entry-render.tsx` connects these semantic events to Entry previews. With a preview provider present, hovering uses the Macro's first source Entry, ordinary clicking pins its preview, and Ctrl-clicking calls the consumer's preview-activation port. Consumer interaction callbacks remain chained into this behavior.

Navigation itself stays outside Basics. `EntryInteractionPorts` receives title activation, source activation with the opaque pointer, preview activation, and block interactions; host adapters decide what those actions mean. `EntryPreviewProvider` recursively renders previews with the supplied drivers, language runtime, hooks, and ports. Thus shared semantic targeting and preview behavior do not require an editor-specific navigation implementation.


## Own-index activation boundary (0.3.6)

An activated semantic node owns its Entry events. Resolve a click or hover from a nested nonsemantic KaTeX/HTML span to the nearest semantic data-tree-path node in the owning render root, then use only that node's own Entry indices (including its resolved Macro source.entries). An unindexed node produces no indexed Entry click/hover or preview, even when a parent is indexed. Never walk past the activated semantic node searching for an ancestor index. Generic semantic callbacks and highlighting remain available for unindexed nodes. An actual activation of the parent still fires its own indices; indexed children retain their own indices. Existing binder navigation/highlighting remains unchanged.

Nested render roots and portal popovers are interaction ownership boundaries: an event owned by an inner root must not be reinterpreted as the outer root's indexed node on click or hover. Nonsemantic nested spans are not new semantic nodes. Tests must cover indexed/unindexed children, direct parent activation, nested KaTeX spans, binder behavior, nested render roots and recursive Entry previews.
